newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's giant OCP to build new plant at $12.8 mln.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's giant OCP to build new plant at $12.8 mln.

text.p: EMAPHOS firm, a subsidiary of Morocco's phosphate giant Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP), and two local banks signed an accord of 110 million dirhams ($12.8 million) to build a purified phosphoric acid plant, the group said on Friday.

Societe Euro Maroc Phosphore (EMAPHOS) was set up as joint venture 50/50 between the OCP and Belgian foam products maker Recticel. BR earlier this year. The firm is presided by the OCP managing director Mourad Cherif.
The two banks are Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, and Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique, the statement said.
"The loan will partly finance the EMAPHOS project which aims to build a purified phosphoric acid plant in Jorf Lasfar," the group said in a statement.
Jorf Lasfar is located on the Atlantic coast, at 200 km south of Rabat.
The plant's production is expected to start in July 1997, it said.

The loan is a part of a credit line provided by the European Bank of Investment to BMCE and BNDE in the framework of the fourth protocole of the financial and technical cooperation between Morocco and the European Union, it said.
The state-run OCP registered a turnover of $1.3 billion dirhams in 1995, officials said.
